trial_court: Family Court, Rourkela, Civil Proceeding No. 132 of 2021
case_name: Nirmal Karnakar vs Parbati @ Parbati Karnakar
facts_of_case: The respondent-wife is an elderly woman with no independent income. She was receiving ₹1,500 per month in maintenance but the Family Court enhanced it to ₹10,000 per month. The husband appealed against this order saying it was beyond what he had sought and that the court didn't properly assess his financial liabilities.

legal_principles.principle: Courts can modify maintenance upon proof of material change in circumstances.
legal_principles.held: It is well established that Courts can modify maintenance upon proof of material change in circumstances.

legal_principles.principle: The amount of maintenance should be such that a wife is able to maintain herself decently and with dignity.
legal_principles.held: The amount of maintenance should be such that a wife is able to maintain herself decently and with dignity.

legal_principles.principle: The Court is not debarred from awarding compensation exceeding the claimed amount.
legal_principles.held: There is no specific restriction under Section 125 Cr. P.C. that the Magistrate cannot award more than the amount claimed in the petition.
cited_cases: Kamaldeep Kaur and Anr. vs. Balwinder Singh, (2005) SCC OnLine P&H 417

legal_principles.principle: The awarded maintenance should be just and proper, considering the husband's financial capacity and the needs of the dependents.
legal_principles.held: The Court noted that the husband was gainfully employed and had a steady income, which justified the enhancement of the maintenance amounts.
cited_cases: G. Amrutha Rao vs. The State of Andhra Pradesh, (2023) Crl.R.C. No. 80

outcome.final_order: The maintenance payable to the respondent-wife was enhanced from ₹1,500 per month to ₹10,000 per month.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
